as_told.title: Majestic 12 documents arrive in a film canister

related.note: Both are about how the first MJ-12 documents reached Shandera and Moore in the 1980s. This telling says they were probably sent from near Kirtland, in Doty's orbit; the story says DIA's Falcon passed on film made by Angleton's chop shop.
Both concern Angleton's part in the MJ12 documents. This telling says Angleton probably leaked them, per Malmgren; the story says his chop shop made them and a DIA officer passed them on.

plain: In the 1980s, the story goes, an intelligence officer code-named Falcon handed two UFO researchers undeveloped 35mm film of the so-called MJ-12 documents. These are papers that describe a secret group called Majestic 12, said to have handled crashed saucers. A scientist who has worked on Pentagon projects, Eric W. Davis, tells Michels that Falcon was an officer of the DIA, the Defense Intelligence Agency, a Pentagon spy agency. He says Falcon was sent to talk with a TV producer named Jaime Shandera and a researcher named Bill Moore. In Davis's account the papers on the film were first-generation documents. He says they were made by James Jesus Angleton's "chop shop", which he calls Angleton's "mole hunting document production factory". A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells a plainer version. He says the papers first turned up in 1984 in a film canister sent to Shandera. Among them, he says, were the Eisenhower briefing document, a paper dated 18 November 1952 that is addressed to Eisenhower, and a so-called Special Operations Manual. UAPGerb says nothing about Falcon, the DIA or Angleton as the source. If Davis is right, the most famous documents in UFO lore would have been produced on purpose by an intelligence operation, whatever they were meant to hide.
